_comment: Where the system reads booking data from. Copy this file to configs/bookings_source.json
(that file is gitignored, because a database address can contain a password) and edit it.
Booking data is OPTIONAL and READ-ONLY: this system never writes to a booking system.
type "csv"    - a CSV export: {"type": "csv", "path": "exports/bookings.csv"}
type "sqlite" - a SQLite file, opened read-only:
{"type": "sqlite", "path": "C:/booking_app/bookings.db",
"query": "SELECT pitch, starts_at, ends_at, ref, state FROM bookings"}
type "sql"    - another database, via SQLAlchemy (install it first, e.g.
uv add sqlalchemy psycopg2-binary   / pymysql / pyodbc):
{"type": "sql", "url": "postgresql://reader:PASSWORD@host:5432/bookings",
"query": "SELECT ..."}
url examples: postgresql://..., mysql+pymysql://user:pw@host/db,
mssql+pyodbc://user:pw@host/db?driver=ODBC+Driver+18+for+SQL+Server
The query must be ONE statement starting with SELECT or WITH. That check only catches
mistakes - it is not security. The real protection is to give this system its own
database user that is granted SELECT on the bookings table and NOTHING else.
Optional, for every type:
columns     - which of YOUR columns holds each value we need. Our names are
field_id, date, start, end, customer_ref, status, entered_by.
Required: field_id, start, end, status (and date, unless start/end
hold full date-times such as 2026-07-11 10:00, which are split for you).
status_map  - your status words -> ours: confirmed, cancelled, no_show, maintenance,
blocked. A no-show is still a sold booking; maintenance/blocked are not.
date_format, time_format, datetime_format - strptime patterns such as %d/%m/%Y
(defaults: YYYY-MM-DD, HH:MM or HH:MM:SS, ISO date-times).
Relative paths are relative to the project folder.
